rationale: This is essentially the archive's "Liquid Organizational Productivity" (oiadp/xsga × net-working-capital) with dp merged into the denominator — a cosmetic denominator tweak of an already-tested 3.5-t signal rather than a new mechanism, and the pooled xsga+dp scaling muddles rather than resolves the SG&A sign ambiguity it claims to address.

This is the most substantively distinct proposal in the batch — it shifts the debt-covered-cash channel from levels/trends to a two-leg one-lag change concordance with a coherent diagnosis of the prior signal's sparse coverage — though the unsmoothed annual DELTAs will be noisy and the second leg conflates cash-flow improvement with current-debt reduction.

Pure leg-swap: both components (oiadp/xsga productivity and NEG TREND(dlc/lct)) already appear in tested archive signals, and the same pairing with oiadp/dp ("Capital-Productive Maturity Improvement") returned a weak ls_talpha of 1.70, so this is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new hypothesis.

Mechanical recombination of two already-evaluated legs ("Worst-Case Claim-Efficient Margin" and the oiadp/dp productivity family); the stated motivation of pairing a strong-alpha leg with a strong-FMB leg is a generic combinatorial argument, not an economic reason the interaction should be sharper.

The second leg is verbatim the archive's "Debt-Service-Resilient EBITDA" constraint and the first is the same xsga+dp variant proposed above, making this a redundant within-batch and within-archive leg swap on a profitability × near-term-debt theme already tested at least four ways.

Direct leg-swap of "Low-Accrual Profit State" (identical accrual leg, oiadp/at replaced by the already-tested oiadp/dp), and the underlying profitability-plus-low-accruals combination is close to a rediscovery of the well-known Sloan accrual and quality-score anomalies.
